battle.name: 鎮壓
battle.brief: 公元271年，羅馬鑄幣廠總監費利西西莫斯因貪污銀料被追查，煽動工人起兵，奪占卡比托利歐丘廠房與軍械庫。皇帝奧勒良自北方發回詔令，禁衛軍與城市守備大隊夾正規軍分遣隊進剿，於卡利亞山將叛軍逐入窄巷殲滅。卡面的羅馬重步兵是清剿骨幹，以大圓盾護身、盾牆逐屋推進，使平亂數日內收場。

kit.name: 羅馬重步兵
kit.history: 分段鎧甲配重盾。羅馬的戰力靠的是補充兵源與補給線，不是靠重裝。

countries: 交戰的兩方都掛著羅馬帝國的旗號，這是三世紀危機末期最典型的首都內亂形態。正方是羅馬帝國的中央政府：皇帝奧勒良本人當時不在羅馬，他正率主力在北意大利、潘諾尼亞與巴爾幹一線對付汪達爾人、茹圖恩吉人、薩爾馬提亞人與哥特人，只能以詔令遙控首都。真正執行鎮壓的是三支羅馬編制：駐首都的禁衛軍、隸屬城市總監的守備大隊（cohortes urbanae），以及皇帝從行省軍團抽調的正規軍分遣隊（vexillationes）。反方是羅馬鑄幣廠的工人與其領袖費利西西莫斯。此人官職為財政總監（rationalis），主管卡比托利歐丘的羅馬主鑄幣廠，慣於挪用原定供製幣的白銀並鑄造成色不足的劣幣。他不是僭主，沒有自豎旗號，叛軍也沒有自己的國家組織：一群有工具、有爐台、熟悉街區的匠人，在領袖受審之後轉為暴民，佔據卡比托利歐丘一帶的廠房、神廟與武器庫，再向城內各處擴散，號召因糧食短缺而躁動的市民與失業者加入。叛軍據說得到部分元老暗中支持，多半與當年支持昆提魯斯當選的一批人有關。外部的壓力同樣真實：帕米拉帝國在埃及的叛動切斷了羅馬城的穀物供應，饑色成為暴動最好的動員口號。叛亂很快被定性為危害元老院與人民、並與外敵遙相呼應的叛國行為，因此鎮壓未經議會程序即以武力執行。
countriesEn: Both sides fought under the banner of the Roman Empire, which made this a typical civil disturbance in the capital of the late third-century crisis. On the imperial side stood the central government of Rome: the emperor Aurelian himself was not in the city, for he was leading his main army in northern Italy, Pannonia and the Balkans against the Vandals, the Juthungi, the Sarmatians and the Goths, and could only direct events in the capital by written rescript. The actual suppression was carried out by three Roman formations: the Praetorian Guard quartered in the capital, the urban cohorts (cohortes urbanae) under the urban prefect, and detachments of regular army (vexillationes) drawn in by the emperor from the legions of the provinces. Against them stood the workers of the Roman mint and their leader Felicissimus. His office was that of rationalis, the senior financial official in charge of the main mint at Rome on the Capitoline Hill; he was accustomed to diverting the silver earmarked for coinage and to striking coins of inferior quality. He was not an usurper and raised no banner of his own, and the rebel force was not a state organisation either: a body of artisans with tools, furnaces and intimate knowledge of the streets turned into a mob once their leader was put on trial; they occupied the workshops, temples and arsenals around the Capitoline and then spread through the city, calling in citizens and porters angered by the shortage of grain. The rebels are said to have had the secret support of some senators, probably those who had backed the election of Quintillus. The external pressure was just as real: the Palmyrene revolt in Egypt had cut off the grain supply of the city of Rome, and hunger was the best mobilisation cry available. The rising was quickly defined as a crime against the Senate and the people, made all the more dangerous by its apparent coordination with enemies abroad, and for that reason it was crushed by force without any procedure before the Senate.
people: 皇帝路基烏斯·多米提烏斯·奧勒良努斯（Lucius Domitius Aurelianus，公元270至275年在位）是這場鎮壓的絕對中心人物。他出身低微，靠軍功與四帝混戰的戰局登上皇位，深知三世紀的皇帝必須同時握有軍隊與城市。270年底他在北意大利清剿汪達爾人、茹圖恩吉人與薩爾馬提亞人，271年1月在皮亞琴察附近遭伏擊敗績，恐慌傳到羅馬；隨後在梅塔羅河畔的法諾之戰與帕維亞之戰連勝，迫使阿勒曼尼人渡回波河，獲「日耳曼尼亞斯 Maximus」的稱號。同一年他率軍越過多瑙河擊敗哥特人，斬其首領坎納巴德斯，再放棄北岸的達西亞，把行省重組為以塞爾迪卡為首府的新達西亞。他遠在戰線上便要處理首都的財政危機，只能靠一紙詔令調兵。費利西西莫斯（Felicissimus）是財政總監（rationalis），掌羅馬鑄幣廠。史家認為廠中白銀被屢次挪用、成色不足的劣幣由他默許甚至主導；奧勒良整頓幣制、下令追查並把他送上公堂，他趁皇帝不在首都、警力空虛之際煽動廠中工人起兵，據史料記載很快被處決。直接動手的是城市總監（praefectus urbi）率領的守備大隊，以及奉詔進城的禁衛軍與正規軍分遣隊。同一時期的北方戰線上，帕米拉與芝諾比亞的叛動在埃及得手，切斷了羅馬城的穀物通道；元老院中反對奧勒良的一批人暗中接應叛軍，社會層面則是領不到足量穀物的市民、匠人與搬運工。任何一位參與者的選擇，都可以由這三層壓力解釋。
peopleEn: The emperor Lucius Domitius Aurelianus, who ruled from 270 to 275, was the absolute centre of this suppression. He came from humble origins and rose to the throne on military merit and the confusion of the war of the four emperors, and he understood perfectly well that a third-century emperor had to hold the army and the city at the same time. In late 270 he campaigned in northern Italy against the Vandals, the Juthungi and the Sarmatians; in January 271 he was defeated in an ambush near Placentia and the panic reached Rome; he then won in succession at the Metaurus, in the battle of Fano, and at Pavia, forcing the Alamanni back across the Po, and received the title Germanicus Maximus. In the same year he led his legions across the Danube, routed the Goths and killed their leader Cannabaudes, and then abandoned Dacia on the northern bank, reorganising the province as the new Dacia Aureliana with Serdica as its capital. Stranded on the front line, he had to cope with the financial crisis in his capital and could do nothing but issue a rescript calling for troops. Felicissimus was the rationalis, the chief financial official in charge of the Roman mint. Historians hold that the silver of the mint was repeatedly embezzled and that the coins of poor metal were tolerated, if not directed, by him; when Aurelian reformed the coinage, ordered an inquiry and put him on trial, he incited the mint workers to revolt while the emperor was far from the city and the city was short of troops, and the sources say he was killed very quickly. Those who actually fought were the urban cohorts led by the urban prefect, together with the Praetorian Guard and the detachments of regular troops sent into the city under the rescript. On the northern front at the same time, the Palmyrene revolt under Zenobia had succeeded in Egypt and cut the grain route to Rome; a group of senators opposed to Aurelian gave the rising quiet support, while at street level the discontent fell on citizens, artisans and porters who could not obtain their full ration of grain. The choice of every single participant can be explained by those three layers of pressure.
kits: 本卡兵器是羅馬重步兵（Legionary）：分段鎧甲（lorica segmentata）配大圓盾（scutum），主兵器為標槍（pilum）與短劍（gladius），腰後再掛一把短刀。街道戰中這套裝備的價值不在防禦而在秩序：士兵列隊前進時互相遮蔽，盾牌疊成連續的曲面，可以擋住來自巷口、屋頂與窗戶的拋射物；標槍在狹窄街道無法拋出，反成累贅，因此重步兵多以短劍破門、以盾牆推進，把每一段街口變成一次單向的推進。叛軍一方是鑄幣廠的匠人，武器就是生產工具：熔爐、坩堝、鐵錘、鐵鉗、裁切用的剪具、量測成色的天平與砝碼，還有搬運金屬錠用的擔架與繩索。廠區本身即是一座小型軍械庫，銅坯、青銅模與銀料都可就地取用，起事者佔據卡比托利歐丘的廠房與軍械庫後，等於取得一批臨時兵器。鎮壓方由三種編制組成：禁衛軍是精銳近衛重裝步兵，裝備與重步兵相同但訓練與裝備供應優先；城市守備大隊為輕裝步兵，裝備小圓盾（parma）、長矛（hasta velitaris）與短重標槍（pila velitaria），專職街巷戰與追捕；皇帝抽調的正規軍分遣隊則把整建重步兵帶進城內，負責佔據要點與封鎖街口。攻城與遠程器械在此役派不上用場，街道縱深不足，火攻風險太高；史料描述的交手方式是在門廊、樓梯與屋頂之間逐屋清剿，圍攻多以封街、合圍與分割包抄完成。馬匹只出現在巡邏與傳令騎兵身上，主戰全靠步行。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is the Roman legionary: segmented plate armour (lorica segmentata) with the large curved shield (scutum), the pilum and the gladius as principal arms, and a short knife hung at the belt. In a street fight the value of this equipment lies less in protection than in order: as the soldiers advanced in line they covered one another, the shields overlapping into a continuous curve able to stop missiles thrown from alley mouths, roofs and windows; the pilum could not be thrown in a narrow street and became an encumbrance, so the legionaries generally broke doors with the gladius and pushed forward behind the shield wall, turning every street mouth into a one-way advance. On the rebel side the arms of the mint workers were their production tools: furnaces, crucibles, hammers, tongs, shears for cutting blanks, balances and weights for testing fineness, plus barrows and ropes for moving metal ingots. The works itself was a small arsenal; copper blanks, bronze dies and silver were all on the spot, so by seizing the workshops and the arsenal of the Capitoline the insurgents had taken a stock of ready improvised weapons. The suppression side was made up of three different organisations. The Praetorian Guard was an elite body of heavy infantry, armed like the legionaries but with priority in training and supply. The urban cohorts were light infantry equipped with the small round shield (parma), the light spear (hasta velitaris) and the heavy javelin (pila velitaria), and their trade was street fighting and pursuit. The detachments of regular troops drawn in by the emperor brought formed legionaries into the city, to seize key points and seal off the streets. Siege and missile engines were of no use: the streets were too shallow for their effect and the risk of fire was too great. The sources describe the fighting as a house-by-house clearance through porticoes, stairways and roofs, with the siege work done by closing streets, pinching off groups and dividing the enemy by encirclement and flanking movement. Horses appeared only with patrols and dispatch riders; the battle itself was fought entirely on foot.
tactics: 費利西西莫斯的起事是一場典型的城市閃電式暴動。鑄幣廠工人集中在卡比托利歐丘一帶，開工與收工時間固定，廠房與倉庫可作堡壘，街道是他們每日走熟的地形。據史料推想，領袖被送上公堂的消息一傳開，工人即以鐵錘、鉗子和爐具武裝起來，趁夜奪取廠區與軍械庫，隨後散入街巷，奪取散落的武器，並以糧食短缺為口號裹挾市民。叛軍並未掌握城外鄉野，也沒有能力離開首都，因此戰局自始至終是城市內的縱深消耗。奧勒良的處置分三步。第一步是穩住軍隊與首都機構：駐首都的禁衛軍與城市守備大隊未受煽動，城防的日常指揮權仍在城市總監手中，這是叛亂沒有迅速擴大的關鍵。第二步是等皇帝從北方抽調正規軍分遣隊入城，作為攻堅骨幹，同時把散兵與被裹挾者與武裝核心分開對待。第三步是進攻部署：守備大隊作先鋒逐段清空街道，封死通向卡比托利歐丘的街口；重步兵分遣隊佔據高地與門廊，居高臨下以短劍與標槍壓制屋頂的抵抗者；正規軍分遣隊守住通向城外的道路，切斷退路。最終決戰在卡利亞山（caelii mons）一帶打成，叛軍被從平原街區壓縮到山丘上的建築群中，寬闊街道變成狹窄巷弄，進攻方以盾牆一次一次向前推，防守方失去縱深與調動空間，逐屋被清。殘餘分子在隨後數日被沿街搜捕，首領與大量支持者被處死，牽涉其中的元老亦被處決。整場戰鬥的技術要點是：不求野戰的殲滅，而以封街、合圍、分割與逐屋清剿，把一場可能拖成內戰的暴亂壓成數日的巷戰。
tacticsEn: The rising of Felicissimus was a typical lightning urban insurrection. The mint workers were concentrated around the Capitoline Hill, their hours of work were fixed, the workshops and storehouses could serve as strongpoints, and the streets were ground they walked every day. As the sources suggest, once the news spread that their leader had been brought before the tribunal, the workers armed themselves with hammers, tongs and furnace tools, seized the works and the arsenal by night, and then scattered into the streets to pick up whatever weapons they could find, calling on citizens with the cry of hunger. The rebels never held the countryside and had no means of leaving the capital, so from first to last the contest was a struggle for depth inside the city. Aurelian's response had three stages. First, the army and the civic institutions of the capital were held steady: the Praetorian Guard and the urban cohorts quartered in the city were not seduced, and the daily command of the defence remained in the hands of the urban prefect, which was the reason the rising did not spread quickly. Second, the emperor drew detachments of regular troops in from the north; they entered the city as the skeleton of the assault, and the authorities distinguished the armed core from stragglers and the coerced. Third came the deployment for the attack: the urban cohorts led, clearing the streets section by section and sealing every approach to the Capitoline; the detachments of heavy infantry occupied the heights and porticoes, pressing the resistance on the roofs from above with gladius and pilum; the regular detachments held the roads leading out of the city and cut off the retreat. The decisive engagement was fought around the Caelian Hill (caelii mons), where the rebels were compressed from the open districts into the massed buildings of the hill, wide streets narrowing into alleys, the attackers pushing forward shield wall by shield wall while the defenders lost both depth and room to manoeuvre and were cleared house by house. In the days that followed, stragglers were hunted street by street; leaders and many followers were executed, and the senators involved were put to death as well. The whole technical lesson of the fight was this: it sought not an annihilation in the open field but the closing of streets, encirclement, division and house-to-house clearance, so that a rising which might have dragged on as a civil war was compressed into a few days of street fighting.
data: 時間：公元271年，屬三世紀危機與奧勒良諸戰役中的一場首都平亂。現存史料只保存年份，未記月日；本檔月份欄依體例填寫，不代表有據。背景數據可對照：271年1月奧勒良在皮亞琴察附近遭伏擊敗績，隨後於梅塔羅河畔的法諾之戰與帕維亞之戰取勝；同年越多瑙河擊敗哥特人、斬首領坎納巴德斯，並放棄達西亞、重設以塞爾迪卡為首府的新達西亞。兵力：叛軍是鑄幣廠工人及其同城同黨，屬城市內部起事，沒有留下任何可信的編制人數記錄，合理的量級是數百至數千人，而非軍隊；鎮壓方為禁衛軍、城市守備大隊與皇帝抽調的正規軍分遣隊，規模與駐軍編制相關，同樣無具體數字留存。損失：《大英百科全書》1911年版引述某些來源，稱此役死傷約七千，該書編者認為此數極可能有所誇大；現代史家一般只作定性描述，不採精確數字。費利西西莫斯本人據載在叛亂初期即被處決。地理：卡比托利歐丘（鑄幣廠所在）至卡利亞山（決戰地）約三公里，兩地皆在城牆線以內。後續工程與制度：奧勒良城牆自271年起興建，環城約十九公里，設十四座城門；配給制度改為發放麵包並加入橄欖油、鹽與豬肉；貨幣方面推出含銀約百分之五的安托尼尼安斯，幣面標記 XXI 或 KA，意思是二十枚新幣所含白銀相當於一枚舊的銀德納里奧斯。羅馬主鑄幣廠一度關閉整頓，帝國各地另設鑄幣廠，首都不再是唯一錢幣來源。帕米拉在埃及的叛動切斷了羅馬城的穀物供應，是本次民怨的重要背景數據。
dataEn: Date: AD 271, a suppression in the capital belonging to the Crisis of the Third Century and to the wars of Emperor Aurelian. The surviving sources preserve only the year and record neither month nor day; the month field of this file is filled in as a matter of format and is not evidence. For comparison, the background data: in January 271 Aurelian was defeated in an ambush near Placentia, then won at the Metaurus in the battle of Fano and at Pavia; in the same year he crossed the Danube, routed the Goths and killed their leader Cannabaudes, abandoned Dacia, and set up the new province of Dacia Aureliana with Serdica as its capital. Strengths: the rebel force was the mint workers and their fellow citizens in the city, an urban rising for which no reliable figures on organisation survive; a plausible order of magnitude is several hundred to a few thousand men, not an army. The suppression side was the Praetorian Guard, the urban cohorts and the detachments of regular troops drawn in by the emperor, whose numbers depended on the garrison establishment and are likewise not recorded. Losses: the 1911 edition of the Encyclopaedia Britannica, citing certain sources, gives about seven thousand casualties for the fighting, but the editors of that volume thought the figure was probably exaggerated; modern historians generally describe the outcome qualitatively and do not accept a precise number. Felicissimus himself is said to have been executed at the very beginning of the rising. Geography: the Capitoline Hill, where the mint stood, lies about three kilometres from the Caelian Hill, the scene of the decisive fight, and both are inside the later wall circuit. Later works and institutions: the Aurelian Walls were begun in 271, about nineteen kilometres in circuit with fourteen gates; the dole system was changed to the distribution of bread with olive oil, salt and pork added; on the monetary side a new antoninianus containing about five per cent silver was introduced, carrying the mark XXI or KA, meaning that twenty of the new coins contained as much silver as one old silver denarius. The main mint at Rome was closed and reorganised for a time and further mints were established in the provinces, so that the capital was no longer the single source of coinage. The Palmyrene revolt in Egypt, which cut the grain supply to the city of Rome, is the essential background against which the discontent of this year must be measured.
cause: 最直接的起因是錢。奧勒良執政後著手整頓三世紀崩壞的財政，羅馬鑄幣廠的積弊因此被掀開：應供製幣的銀料被一再挪用，廠中出品的錢幣成色不足，重量也往往不足，而這一切默許者正是掌廠的財政總監費利西西莫斯。皇帝把他送上公堂，等於直接觸碰首都最能激起共鳴的日常經驗——口袋裡的錢一年比一年輕。企業式的貪瀆被視為謀逆，鎮壓便毫不猶豫。第二層是治理的空檔。皇帝本人不在首都，他正率主力在北意大利、潘諾尼亞與巴爾幹作戰；羅馬城內除了禁衛軍與城市守備大隊，沒有能迅速壓制數千暴民的常備重兵，首都的秩序實際上只靠這兩支部隊維持，財政官僚敢於在最脆弱的時點發難。第三層是饑食與失業。帕米拉帝國在埃及的叛動切斷了羅馬城的穀物供應，麵包配給不足，匠人與搬運工首當其衝；同時叛軍得到部分元老暗中支持，那些人怕的是奧勒良清洗前次皇位爭奪的痕跡。於是財政貪污成了旗幟，饑荒成了號召，元老成了暗中的支持者。更遠的背景是三世紀危機本身：加里寧以來兵將篡位、邊界崩解、瘟疫橫行的羅馬，首都既是帝國最後的堡壘，也是最不設防的地方。費利西西莫斯之亂正是這套體制的反噬——皇帝需要軍隊與城市，城市的秩序卻是由一班靠貪污維生的財政官員維持的。
causeEn: The most immediate cause was money. Once Aurelian took power he set about repairing the finances wrecked by the third century, and the abuses of the Roman mint were laid bare: the silver earmarked for coinage was diverted again and again, the coins that came out of the workshop were short of silver and often short of weight, and the man who tolerated all of this was Felicissimus, the rationalis in charge of the mint. Putting him before the tribunal touched the daily experience of the capital in the sharpest possible way, for the money in one's purse grew lighter every year. Embezzlement on this scale was treated as treason, and the suppression followed without hesitation. The second layer was a gap in governance. The emperor was not in the capital; he was with his main army in northern Italy, in Pannonia and in the Balkans. Apart from the Praetorian Guard and the urban cohorts, Rome had no standing heavy troops capable of crushing several thousand rioters in short order, and the order of the capital in fact rested on those two bodies alone. Financial officials were therefore tempted to strike at the weakest moment. The third layer was hunger and unemployment. The Palmyrene revolt in Egypt had cut the grain supply to the city of Rome, the bread dole was short, and artisans and porters bore the brunt of it; at the same time the rising had the secret support of some senators who feared that Aurelian would purge the traces of the previous struggle for the throne. Financial corruption thus became the banner, famine the call to arms, and the senators the hidden patrons. Further in the background lay the Crisis of the Third Century itself. Since the reign of Gallienus the empire had seen soldier emperors, collapsing frontiers and plague, and Rome was at once the last fortress of the state and its most undefended place. The rising of Felicissimus was the recoil of that system upon itself: the emperor needed the army and the city, while the order of the city was in fact kept by a class of financial officials who lived on embezzlement.
impact: 這場平亂的直接後果是首都秩序的重整。費利西西莫斯被除、鑄幣廠被整頓、涉案元老被處死，羅馬城在很長時間內沒有再出現同等規模的匠人暴動。皇帝同時以詔令褒獎平叛的禁衛軍與城市守備大隊，等於向全帝國宣告首都的暴力機器仍然效忠，強化了他作為三世紀第一位能同時握有軍隊與城市之皇帝的形象。第二個後果最為長久：城牆。叛亂之後，奧勒良把羅馬的防衛看得比以往任何一任皇帝都重，271年開工興建環城約十九公里、設十四座城門的奧勒良城牆，部分利用舊塞維安城牆的塔樓與城內陵墓的石料。這道牆沿用到近代，殘段至今仍嵌在今日羅馬的街廓之中，是羅馬城內保存下來的最大古羅馬建築群之一。第三個後果是貨幣與財政。鑄幣廠整頓與新幣制推出，是三世紀後期第一次認真的幣值整頓；中央鑄幣權因各地增設鑄幣廠而分散，羅馬城不再是帝國唯一的錢幣來源。客觀上這提高了邊疆與行省軍隊就地供應軍餉的能力，也讓地方貨幣與中央貨幣的關係變得鬆散。第四個後果在軍隊政治。皇帝在首都不必事事依賴禁衛軍，守備大隊配合皇帝直屬分遣隊便能解決問題，說明三世紀皇權可以靠常備機構而非宮廷政變維持秩序，為後來戴克里先的軍團分區與禁衛軍廢除埋下伏筆。至於更遠的一層，本次平亂是奧勒良重建帝國的連續動作之一：鎮壓首都的同時，帝國正在帕米拉與埃米薩方向集結，272至273年收復帕米拉、俘虜芝諾比亞之後，奧勒良才佩上世界重建者的名號。首都平亂讓他沒有內患，可以專心東征。
impactEn: The immediate consequence of the suppression was a reordering of the capital. Felicissimus was removed, the mint was reorganised, implicated senators were put to death, and for a long time no artisan rising of comparable scale disturbed Rome again. The emperor rewarded the Praetorian Guard and the urban cohorts for their service by rescript, which announced to the whole empire that the armed instrument of the capital remained obedient, and strengthened his image as the first third-century emperor to hold both the army and the city. The second consequence is the longest lasting: the wall. After the rising, Aurelian cared about the defence of Rome more than any emperor before him, and in 271 he began the Aurelian Walls, about nineteen kilometres in circuit with fourteen gates, built in part from the towers of the old Servian Wall and from the stone of tombs in the city. The circuit remained in use into modern times and its surviving stretches are still built into the blocks of present-day Rome, forming one of the largest preserved groups of ancient Roman structures inside the city. The third consequence lies in currency and finance. The reform of the mint and the introduction of a new coinage were the first serious restoration of the value of money in the later third century; the central monopoly of coinage was broken up as further mints were opened in the provinces, so that Rome was no longer the only source of coin for the empire. In objective terms this made it easier for the armies on the frontiers and in the provinces to be paid locally, and it also loosened the bond between provincial and central money. The fourth consequence belongs to military politics. The emperor in the capital no longer had to depend on the Praetorian Guard for everything; the urban cohorts together with the emperor's own detachments could deal with the emergency. This showed that third-century imperial power could be maintained through standing institutions rather than through palace coups, and it prepared the way for the division of the legions and the abolition of the guard under Diocletian. At a yet greater distance, this suppression was one link in the continuous work by which Aurelian rebuilt the empire: while he pacified the capital the empire was concentrating for the campaign in the direction of Palmyra and Emesa, and only after the reconquest of Palmyra and the capture of Zenobia in 272 and 273 did he assume the title of restorer of the world. The suppression in the capital left him without civil war behind him and free to concentrate on the eastern march.
result: 費利西西莫斯在起事初期即被處決，暴動的核心在起事階段便失去領袖。叛軍主力佔據卡比托利歐丘的廠房與軍械庫後向城內擴散，被禁衛軍與城市守備大隊聯手封街分割，在皇帝抽調入城的正規軍分遣隊投入後，於卡利亞山被壓入狹窄街巷殲滅；其後數日，殘餘武裝被沿街搜捕，參與者或處死或流放，牽涉在內的元老同樣被處死。叛亂全程局限於首都城內，沒有演變成與奧勒良正面的內戰，也沒有演變成第二次佩勒尼庇烏斯式的準獨立運動。奧勒良的實際戰果，是一場在數日之內平定的首都暴動。善後工作緊接著展開。羅馬主鑄幣廠關閉整頓，工人與官員重新審核，帝國各地增設鑄幣廠使中央壟斷的貨幣供應被打破；同時推出含銀約百分之五的新安托尼尼安斯，幣面標記 XXI 或 KA，並以收回舊劣幣的方式推動新幣。配給制度同樣在這一年改為麵包並加入橄欖油、鹽與豬肉，以應付帕米拉斷糧後的首都供應壓力。最後是防禦。奧勒良城牆在271年開工，把卡比托利歐與卡利亞山兩處衝突地點一併圈進同一道防線。事件本身的結局是一次鎮壓成功，但它把三個問題同時攤在案上：鑄幣廠的貪污、首都的糧食、以及城防的空洞。三件事在同一年內由同一個人著手處理，這才是271年羅馬城真正的收場。
resultEn: Felicissimus was executed at the very start of the rising, so the movement lost its leader while it was still being organised. The main body of the rebels, having seized the workshops and the arsenal of the Capitoline, spread into the city; the Praetorian Guard and the urban cohorts joined hands to close the streets and divide them, and once the detachments of regular troops brought in by the emperor entered the city, the rebels were compressed into the narrow alleys of the Caelian Hill and annihilated. In the days that followed the remaining armed men were hunted street by street, participants were executed or exiled, and the senators involved were put to death as well. The rising remained confined to the city throughout; it did not turn into a civil war against Aurelian on open terms, nor did it become a second quasi-independent movement of the kind Pelagius had led. Aurelian's actual gain was a capital insurrection brought to an end in a matter of days. The settlement followed at once. The main mint at Rome was closed and reorganised, the workers and officials were reviewed, and the opening of further mints in the provinces broke the central monopoly of the coin supply; at the same time a new antoninianus containing about five per cent silver was introduced, marked XXI or KA, and pushed into circulation by the recall of the old base coins. The dole system too was changed in that same year to bread with olive oil, salt and pork added, to meet the pressure on the supply of the capital after the Palmyrene cut of the grain. Last came defence. In 271 work began on the Aurelian Walls, which drew the two places of conflict, the Capitoline and the Caelian Hill, inside a single line. The event itself ended in a successful suppression, but it laid three problems on the table at once: the embezzlement at the mint, the grain of the capital, and the emptiness of the city's defences. All three were taken in hand within the same year by the same man, and that is the real conclusion of the year 271 for the city of Rome.
